sections.html:
Foley is a city in Baldwin County in the far south of Alabama, and it is one of the principal cities of the Daphne-Fairhope-Foley metropolitan area, which covers all of Baldwin County. It sits at about 62 feet above sea level, uses area code 251, and has ZIP codes 36535 and 36536.

The best-known intersection is where U.S. Route 98 meets Alabama Highway 59. The city's motto is "The Heart of the American Riviera," and its nickname is "The Forward City."

For a house seller, the location means Foley draws both local buyers and people relocating to the Gulf Coast, and the market can look quite different from inland Alabama towns.

sections.h2: How did Foley grow from a railroad town?
sections.html:
Foley was founded by John B. Foley of Chicago, who bought between 40,000 and 50,000 acres of land in south Baldwin County after hearing about it from a railroad agent in 1901. He formed the Magnolia Springs Land Company, laid track from Bay Minette with his own money, and saw the first station built in 1905.

The original station burned in 1908 and was replaced the next year. That building is now the city museum. Foley was incorporated in 1915, with G. I. Weatherly as its first mayor.

The census counts show how fast the place has grown since then, and fast growth usually means a mix of new construction and older houses competing for the same buyers.

sections.h2: Who lives in Foley and what do the housing numbers say?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 8,799 households in Foley, and the median age was 48.5. About 28.6 percent of residents were 65 or older.

The same census found 9,911 housing units with 11.2 percent vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 2.4 percent and the rental vacancy rate was 10.3 percent. Census vacancy counts can include second homes and rentals, and sellers of those properties face different choices than full-time residents.

  • Households in 2020: 8,799, of which 46.8 percent were married-couple households
  • About 28.8 percent of households were people living alone
  • With that age profile, some owners may be weighing a move or an estate sale

sections.h2: What is OWA and how does it affect the area?
sections.html:
OWA is a 520-acre resort and entertainment destination in Foley, owned and operated by the Poarch Band of Creek Indians. It opened in 2017 near the South McKenzie Street commercial corridor and has a shopping and dining area called Downtown OWA, an amusement park and a water park, Tropic Falls, whose first phase opened in June 2022.

Large attractions bring jobs, traffic and short-term visitors, and they can change what nearby neighborhoods are worth to different kinds of buyers. If your house is close to the McKenzie Street corridor, an investor may value it differently than a family looking for a quiet street.

Foley also has smaller local draws, including the Antique Rose Trail with over 500 varieties of roses, the City of Foley Museum in the restored train depot, and the Holmes Medical Museum, which was the first hospital in Baldwin County.

Foley is part of Baldwin County Public Schools. The city is served by Foley High School for grades 9 to 12 and Foley Middle School for grades 7 and 8.

  • Foley Elementary School (K-6)
  • Florence B. Mathis Elementary (K-6)
  • Magnolia Elementary (K-6)
  • Swift Consolidated Elementary (K-6)

The county school system, not a separate city district, runs these schools, so attendance zones follow county rules. Buyers with children often ask about zoning before they make an offer, so be ready to point them to the county school office.

sections.h2: How do people get around Foley?
sections.html:
Foley is built around car travel. U.S. 98 and Highway 59 are the main routes through town. Countywide dial-a-ride service is provided by the Baldwin Regional Area Transit System, known as BRATS.

Houses with easy access to the main routes and the commercial corridor are generally simpler to market than those on long rural roads.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Foley?
sections.html:
Alabama's recordation tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value on a deed, set by Alabama Code 40-22-1. A $300,000 sale would owe $300 in deed tax, and the probate office also collects its own recording fee.

The deed must be accompanied by a state form attesting to the actual purchase price. Intentionally withholding that proof after the probate office asks can add a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax due, whichever is greater.

  • The judge of probate records the deed in the county where the property sits
  • Deed tax is usually paid at closing by the party the contract names
  • A title company or attorney prepares the deed and checks the title

sections.h2: When are property taxes due on a Foley house?
sections.html:
Alabama's Department of Revenue says the lien date is October 1 and the tax is due the following October 1, with delinquency after December 31. All taxable real property except public utilities is assessed at the local level by the county.

If you sell in the middle of the year, the title company usually prorates the tax so each side pays for the days it owned the house. Check whether the current year's bill has been paid before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What paperwork should a Foley seller gather before a sale?
sections.html:
Start with the recorded deed, your latest tax bill and any mortgage statement, because those three documents answer most of a buyer's early questions. Foley sits in Baldwin County, so recorded deeds are filed with the county probate office.

  • The deed or trust paperwork showing who owns the house
  • A payoff figure from any lender with a lien
  • Names of anyone else on title, such as heirs or a former spouse
  • Utility and insurance details if the house is empty

A title company will find liens or ownership gaps before closing, and it is better to learn about them early than on the day you planned to sign.

sections.h2: What options does a Foley seller have?
sections.html:
Foley sellers can list on the open market, sell on their own, or take a cash offer. A listing may reach more buyers but needs showings, repairs and a buyer who qualifies for a loan.

  • With a listing, expect to prepare the house, wait for offers and negotiate after inspection.
  • A private sale saves a commission but you handle all of the paperwork and screening.
  • A cash purchase from Cash Home Buyers is made as-is, so you do not need to repair or clean for showings.

Owners of inherited houses, rentals with problems and homes that need work often prefer the cash route because it limits the steps between deciding to sell and closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Foley house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases the house in its current condition and accounts for repairs in the price. A title company or attorney can tell you what must be disclosed.

faqs.q: How much is deed tax in Baldwin County?
faqs.a: The state rate is 50 cents per $500 of value, so a $250,000 house owes $250. The county probate office adds a recording fee.

faqs.q: When is the property tax bill due in Foley?
faqs.a: Alabama property tax is due October 1 and becomes delinquent after December 31. At a sale, the title company normally prorates it.

faqs.q: Who handles the closing for a Foley sale?
faqs.a: A title company or attorney usually handles it. The probate office records the deed but cannot draft one for you.
The Census Bureau counted 20,335 people in 2020 and estimates 30,354 for 2025, so the city has been expanding quickly.

faqs.q: Will a cash offer be higher than a listing price?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. A cash offer is usually lower than a fully prepared retail sale, but it removes repair costs, showings and delays. Compare the net amount you would keep.

faqs.q: What if I own a vacant house in Foley?
faqs.a: You can still sell it. Gather the deed and tax bill, and keep insurance and utilities active until closing. A cash buyer can view the property as it stands.
